reason: Both responses share the right core design: verbatim safety fields, banned-claim checks, risk tiering and a no-unreviewed-AI-copy fallback. Response 1 is better because it validates its checks with planted-bad and clean controls, sets zero-tolerance stop conditions, treats the 50-page batch as unverified rather than a catalog-wide error rate, names who each harm affects, and leaves the applicable rules for counsel to identify. Response 2 is more concretely tiered, but it asserts specific FDA/FTC duties, presents the 50-page batch as yielding a 'real error rate', offers unsourced workload estimates, and omits AI disclosure.
